list: the official 55 trophies, frozen 2026-11-18 (Exophase and PSNProfiles agree on every name, description and grade)
sources: Official list on Exophase (names, descriptions, grades); PSNProfiles (PSN progress targets); guides are our own words from the official descriptions, not yet checked in the game

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum. It pops the moment the other 54 trophies are earned — there is nothing extra to do beyond them. Use the Roadmap tab and work stage by stage; the long grinds (250 stunts, 100 WAiNK spots, 52 areas) are the real boss fight, so start them early and let them tick over while you play the story.
steps: Earn the other 54 trophies in any order.
Check the Roadmap tab for the order that wastes the least replaying.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Unmissable story trophy. Play the opening mission Gone Fishing to its end and the trophy pops at the mission-complete screen. Nothing to prepare — it is the game's first mission.
steps: Start the game and play Gone Fishing through to the end.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Unmissable story trophy. Finish every mission in Chapter 1; the trophy pops when the chapter closes. If you are mopping up later, chapter trophies follow story progress only — side content does not count toward them.
steps: Complete all Chapter 1 missions in order.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Unmissable story trophy. Finish every mission in Chapter 2; it pops when the chapter closes. The name is printed exactly as PlayStation publishes it, asterisks included.
steps: Complete all Chapter 2 missions in order.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Unmissable story trophy. Finish every mission in Chapter 3; it pops when the chapter closes. By now the stranger strands and side activities are open — start the long grinds (stunts, exploration) between missions rather than leaving them all for after the story.
steps: Complete all Chapter 3 missions in order.
Between missions, bank stunts and explore new areas toward the grind trophies.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Unmissable story trophy. Finish every mission in Chapter 4; it pops when the chapter closes. Before the final stretch, glance at the Missables tab — a few trophies only happen in one situation, and the endgame is the wrong time to discover that.
steps: Complete all Chapter 4 missions in order.
Check the Missables tab before the final mission.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Gold story trophy. Complete the final mission and it pops at the credits. It is unmissable as long as you finish the story, but do the missable trophies first — after the finale, some one-time moments may be gone.
steps: Finish every missable-flagged trophy you still need.
Then complete the final mission.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Story mission trophy. Play the mission Breakfast Run to completion; it pops at the mission-complete screen. Mission trophies are tied to the mission itself, so there is no side requirement — just finish it.
steps: Play Breakfast Run when it appears in the story.
Complete it to the mission-complete screen.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Story mission trophy. Complete The Cartel Heist and it pops at the mission-complete screen. Heist missions tend to be long with several stages — expect checkpoints rather than a single run, and finish the whole mission in one sitting if you can.
steps: Play The Cartel Heist when it appears in the story.
Complete every stage to the mission-complete screen.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Story mission trophy. Complete the mission Child's Play and it pops at the mission-complete screen. No preparation needed beyond reaching it in the story.
steps: Play Child's Play when it appears in the story.
Complete it to the mission-complete screen.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Story mission trophy. Complete the mission Headliners and it pops at the mission-complete screen. The title is stylised exactly as PlayStation publishes it.
steps: Play Headliners when it appears in the story.
Complete it to the mission-complete screen.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Story mission trophy. Complete the mission VCIA Takedown and it pops at the mission-complete screen. VCIA is the airport, so expect this one to involve the airport area — the mission name is all the official description gives, and anything more specific is not yet checked in the game.
steps: Play VCIA Takedown when it appears in the story.
Complete it to the mission-complete screen.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Story mission trophy. Complete the mission Operation Savage Glory and it pops at the mission-complete screen. The name suggests a set-piece mission — take it at full health and with stocked ammo, as you would any late-story operation.
steps: Play Operation Savage Glory when it appears in the story.
Complete it to the mission-complete screen.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Gold trophy for 100% completion. This is the platinum's real gate: it means finishing the story, the stranger strands, the activities, the collectibles and the challenges the game counts toward 100%. The in-game stats screen is the authority on what still counts — check it whenever the trophy feels far away, and clear one category at a time instead of wandering. Expect this to be the last gold before the platinum.
steps: Finish the story and all stranger strands.
Clear every activity, collectible set and challenge the stats screen counts toward 100%.
Check the in-game completion percentage after each category.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Silver grind trophy: pull off 250 stunts. Stunts are the game's jump, airtime and near-miss style moves — start counting from your first hour, because 250 is a lot to leave for the endgame. Fast cars, ramps and long straight roads with traffic to thread are your friends; a stunt only counts when the game registers it, so vary the move rather than repeating one trick in one spot and assuming it stacks.
steps: Do stunts from the start of the game — jumps, airtime, near misses.
Check your stunt count in the stats screen as you go.
Grind the remainder on open roads with ramps once the story is done.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 250 stunts); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sampler trophy: try each of the 9 activity types once. You do not need to win or master any of them — one attempt at each type is enough. Work through the activity list methodically and tick each type off as you try it; this pairs naturally with the other activity trophies, since every attempt also feeds their counts.
steps: Open the activities list and try one of each of the 9 types.
One attempt each is enough — no win required.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 9 activity types); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Silver skill trophy: gold medals in all 42 Shooting Range challenges. This is the hardest pure-skill trophy on the list for most players. Learn one weapon class at a time, use the range's practice runs to learn the target patterns before chasing gold, and save the trickiest challenges for when your aim is warm. Gold thresholds are per challenge, so a bad run costs nothing but time — retry freely.
steps: Unlock the Shooting Range and learn each challenge's targets in practice.
Gold the easiest weapon classes first to learn the scoring.
Return for the hardest challenges with warmed-up aim; retrying is free.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 42 Shooting Range challenges); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations. Each location is a separate race to win — one win per location, not 14 wins at one spot. Learn the course on a first run, then race to win; drone handling rewards smooth lines over top speed, so cut corners cleanly rather than boosting into walls.
steps: Find each of the 14 Top Fun drone race locations.
Win one race at each location (one win per location).
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 14 locations); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word different matters: the same race won twice counts once. Spread your wins across race types and locations, and keep a mental note (or a note in this guide) of which races you have already won so you do not waste wins on repeats.
steps: Win races across different types and locations.
Track which races you have won — repeats do not count.
20 different wins pops the trophy.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Cal is a rival angler, so this is a head-to-head fishing contest, not free fishing. Learn the fishing mechanics first on your own — casting, reeling and keeping the line's tension in the safe zone — then challenge Cal when you can land fish consistently. If you lose, challenge him again; the description promises no one-shot limit.
steps: Learn fishing basics first (cast, reel, manage line tension).
Take the fishing challenge against Cal and out-fish him.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game. Find an arcade, pick any game, and play it through to its end — finishing is what counts, not a high score. If a game has multiple rounds or levels, you need to see it through to the end screen.
steps: Find an arcade and start any arcade game.
Play it through to completion.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Stranger-strand trophy. Find Andy, play through his whole mission strand, and complete his final mission. Stranger strands unlock as you explore and progress the story — if Andy has no mission marker yet, keep playing the story and checking the map.
steps: Find Andy and start his mission strand.
Complete every mission in the strand, ending with his final one.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Stranger-strand trophy. Find Kenton, play through his whole mission strand, and complete his final mission. The title hints at boats — expect water to feature in his strand, though the official description says nothing more specific, and that is not yet checked in the game.
steps: Find Kenton and start his mission strand.
Complete every mission in the strand, ending with his final one.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Stranger-strand trophy. Find Billy, play through his whole mission strand, and complete his final mission. The title suggests riding solo — likely bikes feature in his strand, though that is not pinned down by the official description and is not yet checked in the game.
steps: Find Billy and start his mission strand.
Complete every mission in the strand, ending with his final one.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Silver strand trophy: complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida. Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each have one, so you need three more beyond them. Explore the whole state — strands are scattered across Leonida, not clustered in Vice City — and talk to every stranger marker you see. A strand only counts when its final mission is done.
steps: Complete the strands for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone.
Find and finish 3 more stranger strands anywhere in Leonida.
A strand counts only when its final mission is complete.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 8 strands); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Stranger-strand trophy. Find Randy, play through his whole mission strand, and complete his final mission. The title suggests moving goods — expect supply runs in his strand, though the official description says nothing more specific, and that is not yet checked in the game.
steps: Find Randy and start his mission strand.
Complete every mission in the strand, ending with his final one.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Stranger-strand trophy. Find Tyrone, play through his whole mission strand, and complete his final mission. The title suggests spinning — wheels, records or otherwise — but that is not pinned down by the official description and is not yet checked in the game.
steps: Find Tyrone and start his mission strand.
Complete every mission in the strand, ending with his final one.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida. These are scenic spots scattered across the whole state, so this is an exploration trophy as much as a collectible one — visit viewpoints, beaches, hilltops and quiet corners. Meditate at each spot once; the trophy pops at the 18th. Use the in-game map and your notes here to track which spots you have done.
steps: Find meditation spots across Leonida (viewpoints, beaches, hilltops).
Meditate at each one — 18 in total.
Track visited spots in this guide's notes so none is missed.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 18 spots); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret's strand leads to a one-of-a-kind animal hunt — the description's word unique means there is a specific animal to find, not just any wildlife. Follow Bret's missions until the hunt is offered, then track the animal patiently: approach quietly, watch the wind and the terrain if the game models them, and take a clean shot. Losing the trail should let you try again, but treat the first attempt as the one that counts.
steps: Play Bret's strand until the hunt is offered.
Track the unique animal and take it down.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Silver collectible trophy: complete 3 collectible card sets. Cards are hidden across Leonida — in shops, interiors, side streets and out-of-the-way spots — and a set only counts when every card in it is found. Collect as you explore rather than in one sweep at the end; a set's missing card is much easier to find when you remember roughly where you have already looked.
steps: Collect cards as you explore Leonida.
Complete all cards in a set — 3 full sets pops the trophy.
Note each set's missing cards in this guide so you can hunt them down.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Silver grind trophy: use WAiNK It at 100 locations. WAiNK It is the game's check-in style feature — do it everywhere you go, not just at landmarks. Make it a habit: every new area, shop, beach and viewpoint gets a WAiNK It before you leave. At 100 locations this is one of the longest passive grinds, so start on day one and never pass a spot without doing it.
steps: WAiNK It at every new location you visit, from the first hour.
Do it at landmarks, shops, beaches and viewpoints — anywhere it is offered.
100 locations pops the trophy.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 100 locations); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's small side goals — scattered across activities, combat, driving and exploration — and they stack up naturally if you play broadly. Check the challenges menu often: it tells you which ones are close to done, and knocking out the near-complete ones first keeps the count climbing. Any 50 count, so favour the easy ones.
steps: Open the challenges menu and note the near-complete ones.
Clear the easiest challenges first across all categories.
50 completed challenges pops the trophy.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.missableNote: Needs your partner beside you and a 4-star wanted level — a situation that only happens while your partner is with you. If you finish the story sections where your partner rides along, the moment may be gone. Do it the first time you have your partner and a clear escape route.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, build a 4-star wanted level, then lose the cops and escape. Plan the escape before the heat: know where the alleys, tunnels and water are, and break line of sight before the search tightens. Your partner must be with you when the wanted level clears — do not ditch them mid-chase.
steps: Have your partner with you.
Build a 4-star wanted level.
Break line of sight and escape until the wanted level clears — with your partner still beside you.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.missableNote: Needs your partner beside you for three robberies in a row while the wanted level never drops. If the story stops pairing you with your partner, the moment may be gone. Do it the first time you have your partner and three shops close together.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob three shops in a row without the wanted level ever clearing in between — the chain breaks if you lose the heat. Pick three shops close together, hit them fast, and keep moving: lingering in one place lets the cops close in. A fast getaway car parked nearby helps more than a big gun here.
steps: Have your partner with you and pick 3 shops close together.
Rob the first, then the second, then the third — without losing the wanted level between them.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles. Discovery means encountering new vehicle types — driving, parking or just getting close to a new model should register it, though the exact trigger is not pinned down by the official description and is not yet checked in the game. Variety is the strategy: car parks, dealerships, docks, airfields and traffic in different districts each hide models you have not seen yet.
steps: Drive through different districts, car parks, docks and airfields.
Encounter new vehicle types — 100 discovered pops the trophy.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Down 5 enemies in one use of Combat Focus. Wait for a fight with at least five enemies grouped together — a gang shootout or a mission firefight — then trigger Combat Focus and chain the kills before it ends. Do not waste it on two stragglers: patience for a crowded fight is the whole trick. If the meter runs out at four, reload the checkpoint and try again.
steps: Find a fight with 5+ enemies grouped together.
Trigger Combat Focus and down 5 of them before it ends.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missableNote: A one-time-style stunt at the airport (VCIA): leave in a way no schedule covers — a stolen plane, or a runway exit that is not a flight. The airport is open world, so it may be repeatable, but treat the first attempt as the one that counts and save before you try.
trophies.guide: At VCIA airport, make an unscheduled departure — take a plane that is not yours, or leave the airport by a route no timetable covers. The description is deliberately playful, so the exact trigger is not pinned down by it and is not yet checked in the game; a stolen aircraft leaving the runway is the plainest reading. Save before you try, in case the first attempt does not register.
steps: Go to VCIA airport.
Take an aircraft (or another unscheduled exit) and leave the airport by it.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.missableNote: Rhinos are tanks — they only appear at high wanted levels or in specific missions. If you finish the story missions that feature them, finding one again may be hard. Do it the first time tanks roll in.
trophies.guide: Deal with Rhinos — the game's tanks. They show up at high wanted levels or in missions that feature armour, so this trophy is about surviving the encounter: keep moving, use cover and heavy weapons, and do not try to fight a tank head-on in a sedan. The official description is a joke, not instructions, so the exact trigger (destroy one? survive one? steal one?) is not yet checked in the game — engaging a Rhino aggressively is the best first attempt.
steps: Reach a high wanted level or a mission where Rhinos appear.
Engage the Rhino — destroy it or survive the encounter.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.missableNote: A clean, undetected robbery — one alarm or one witness and the attempt fails. Jewelry stores can be robbed again, but a failed attempt may raise the heat for the next one. Plan it, save first, and go at a quiet hour.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Scout it first: cameras, guards, sightlines and the exit. Go quiet — no alarms, no witnesses, no smashed glass in front of a guard. If you are spotted, the attempt is blown; leave, let the heat die, and try again with a better plan.
steps: Scout a jewelry store: cameras, guards, exit.
Rob it without being detected — no alarms, no witnesses.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Silver crime trophy: rob 5 bank vaults and escape each time. Each vault is a job of its own — plan the entry, the vault itself and the getaway, because escaping is part of the trophy: a vault cracked with no escape does not count. Spread the five across the game so you are never grinding vaults back-to-back with the same heat.
steps: Rob a bank vault and escape — the escape counts.
Repeat for 5 vaults in total.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 5 bank vaults); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks run set routes through the city — spot one, stop it, crack it and get out before the response arrives. The getaway matters as much as the robbery: have an escape car ready and a route that breaks line of sight fast.
steps: Find an armored truck on its route.
Stop it, rob it, and escape before the response closes in.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida. This is the map-completion trophy: every named area in the state counts, from Vice City districts to the far corners of Leonida. The in-game map is the authority on what is left — sweep it district by district, and visit the edges (beaches, swamps, islands) that are easy to skip. Pair it with the meditation spots and WAiNK check-ins, which pull you to the same far-flung places.
steps: Open the map and note unexplored areas.
Visit all 52 areas of Leonida, including beaches, swamps and islands.
Pair the sweep with meditation spots and WAiNK check-ins.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 52 areas); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the 9 gangs. Every gang in Leonida runs illegal operations — find one per gang and hit it. The gangs are spread across the state, so this trophy doubles as a tour of their territories; note which gang each operation belonged to as you go, so you do not hit the same gang twice and wonder why the count stalls.
steps: Find illegal operations across gang territories.
Rob one operation for each of the 9 gangs.
Track which gangs you have hit — repeats do not count.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 9 gangs); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.missableNote: A quiet moment at a specific place: a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. It may need a particular bar or a particular time of day, and the game may only offer the moment once. Do it the first time you are on Ocean Beach with a bar in view — do not assume it waits.
trophies.guide: Go to Ocean Beach, find a spot with a view — a beach bar or a waterfront seat — and enjoy a cocktail there. This is a vibes trophy, not a grind: slow down, order the drink, and let the moment register. If nothing pops at the first bar, try another beachfront spot; the official description names Ocean Beach, not a specific bar, and that detail is not yet checked in the game.
steps: Go to Ocean Beach.
Find a beachfront bar or viewpoint and enjoy a cocktail there.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.missableNote: Smashing out of a showroom in classic style — a one-time set-piece moment, likely tied to a mission or a first visit. Once the showroom's glass is gone, the moment may not repeat. Save before you try it.
trophies.guide: Get into a vehicle showroom and smash your way out in classic style — through the glass, in a car, the way the old games taught us. The description is a nod, not a manual: pick a showroom, pick a fast car, and drive out through the front. If the first attempt does not register, try another showroom; the exact trigger is not yet checked in the game.
steps: Find a vehicle showroom.
Drive out through the showroom front in a vehicle.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. The name is printed with the curly apostrophe exactly as PlayStation publishes it. Follow-through means completing the bowling action properly — play a frame or a full game at this specific alley, not just any bowling lane. If one game does not pop it, finish a full game.
steps: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Play bowling there — a full game if a single frame does not count.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: A partnership moment with mass appeal. The description is deliberately vague — it reads like a story beat where the partnership does something big in public. Play the story with your partner and this should come naturally; if it has not popped by the late game, check the story missions you may have rushed past. Anything more specific is not pinned down by the official description and is not yet checked in the game.
steps: Play the story partnership missions.
Watch for a big public moment with your partner.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.missableNote: PSN tracks choices to a count of 500 — and choices, by definition, cannot all be made in one playthrough if some are exclusive. Pick deliberately, and know that a second playthrough or mission replay may be needed for the choices you did not take.
trophies.guide: Make choices — PSN tracks them toward a count of 500. Choices appear in missions, conversations and stranger strands, so play attentively and pick deliberately instead of mashing through dialogue. Because some choices are exclusive, this is the trophy most likely to need a second pass: keep a note of the big choices you made, and plan a replay for the ones you did not take.
steps: Make choices in missions, conversations and stranger strands.
PSN counts them toward 500 — keep choosing, and plan a replay for exclusive choices you skipped.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 500 choices); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.missableNote: Second time's the charm — this only happens after a first failure at something. If the thing it refers to is a one-time event, the retry window is the moment itself. Fail once, then succeed on the very next try.
trophies.guide: Succeed on a second try. The description says the charm is in the retry: fail at something, then succeed at the same thing on the next attempt. The official description does not name what that something is, and it is not yet checked in the game — the honest read is that a failed attempt followed immediately by a successful retry is the trigger, so when you fail at a challenge, retry it at once instead of walking away.
steps: Fail at a challenge or attempt.
Retry it immediately and succeed on the second try.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.missableNote: A strange event — the kind you stumble on once, at a specific place or time. Random or rare events do not wait for you. Explore odd corners of Leonida, at night as well as by day, and take the strange encounter when it appears.
trophies.guide: Witness something strange. This is the game's weird-encounter trophy — the description is a reaction, not directions, and the event it refers to is not pinned down by the official description and is not yet checked in the game. Explore Leonida's odd corners (the swamps, the desert roads, the far beaches) at different times of day, and when something strange happens, stay and watch it through.
steps: Explore Leonida's odd corners at different times of day.
When a strange event happens, stay and see it through.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.missableNote: A melee drive-by — attacking from a moving vehicle with a melee weapon. It needs a target, a vehicle and a swing to line up at once. It is repeatable in free roam, but do it as soon as you can: it is the kind of trick you forget until the endgame.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by: attack with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle. Drive slowly past a target on foot, swing as you pass, and let the vehicle's speed do the rest. A quiet street with pedestrians and a slow car is the setup; a highway at full speed is not. The description says bowl 'em over — one clean knockdown is the goal.
steps: Equip a melee weapon and get in a vehicle.
Drive slowly past a target on foot and strike with the melee weapon as you pass.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are dirty money from jobs — your contacts clean them for a cut, and the laundered total is what counts, so the grind is earning the bills as much as washing them. Keep a steady pipeline: jobs for bills, contacts for laundering, and never let bills sit unlaundered while you chase the next job.
steps: Earn Marked Bills from jobs.
Launder them through your contacts.
$250,000 laundered in total pops the trophy.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Every shop counts — clothes, food, weapons, car parts, all of it — so this trophy fills itself if you actually use the shops instead of hoarding cash. Buy the gear you need as you need it, and the total climbs on its own; only grind it at the end if you are short, by buying big-ticket items you will use anyway.
steps: Spend in any shops — clothes, food, weapons, car parts.
$100,000 spent in total pops the trophy.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: $100,000); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties. Garages are property purchases scattered across Leonida — each one is a place to store your vehicles, and the trophy wants the full set. Save up and buy them as you find them rather than in one expensive sweep, and check the property listings whenever you are in a new district.
steps: Find garage properties for sale across Leonida.
Purchase all 8 of them.
trophies.sources: Official list on Exophase (name, description, grade); PSNProfiles (PSN count: 8 garages); our own advice from the official description, not yet checked in the game.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. The app is the in-game vehicle service — open it, register a vehicle you own or have found, and repeat for 10 different vehicles. Variety helps: different types and models, not the same car ten times. If a registration does not take, check that the vehicle is actually yours to register.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app.
Register 10 different vehicles through it.
